identity.name: Captaincy General of Cuba
alt_names: Capitanía General de la Isla de Cuba

land.text: the island of Cuba, reorganised in 1607 'as part of Habsburg Spain's attempt to better defend and administer its Caribbean possessions'

predecessors.note: polities.csv has no Cuba-only colonial row; Cuba is presumably inside the Spanish Empire and Kingdom of Spain rows (not checked shape by shape); this dossier is the colony alone.

land.text: the Military Government of Cuba, the infobox successor of 1898

successors.note: Treaty of Paris of 10 December 1898; Cuba's independence as the Republic of Cuba followed on 20 May 1902 (republic-of-cuba dossier). fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): the Military Government of Cuba is a US occupation, not a transfer of sovereignty ('Spain relinquished all claims of sovereignty over and title to Cuba', Treaty of Paris page), so no cell passes to the United States at the end: ledger/14 is a loss to nobody and united-states-of-america/ledger/83 records the occupation.

capitals.name: Havana (San Cristóbal de la Habana)
capitals.note: Infobox "Capital: Havana (San Cristóbal de la Habana)", no dates given.

correction.text: the island of Cuba under the Captain General at Havana, 'created in 1607'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Cuba-only colonial row. The page gives no area; the gazetteer resolves Cuba to 507 cells, about 128,200 km2. The 1764 restructuring added 'the provinces of Florida and Louisiana' to the captaincy for administration; those lands are drawn in the spanish-florida and spanish-louisiana dossiers, not here, and the page gives no date for when each left. The British occupation of the west in 1762-1763 is a ledger overlay (occupation events), not a change of this shape.

region.text: the island of Cuba, 'created in 1607 as part of Habsburg Spain's attempt to better defend and administer its Caribbean possessions'

ledger.note: 1607: Spain sets up the Captaincy General of Cuba at Havana. Infobox 'Administrative reorganisation: 1607'; 'created in 1607 as part of Habsburg Spain's attempt to better defend and administer its Caribbean possessions'. The page gives the year, not the limits.

region.text: the western part of the island round Havana: 'controlled the western part of the island for a year'; the page names no province, so Havana, Artemisa and Mayabeque are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1762: Britain captures Havana and holds the west. 'The British captured Havana after a three-month siege and controlled the western part of the island for a year'; the page lists the 'Siege of Havana (1762)'. Month 8 comes from the Siege of Havana page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Havana: the siege ended with the honours of war on 13 August and 'British forces entered Havana on 14 August' 1762), not from this page. Neither page names the towns held beyond Havana, so the extent is the researcher's reading at confidence 2.

region.text: the western part of the island round Havana, returned to Spain by the Treaty of Paris of 1763

ledger.note: 1763: Cuba returns to Spain. 'Britain returned Cuba in exchange for Florida in the Treaty of Paris' (1763). The page gives no month; the Siege of Havana page gives two that disagree (Havana 'returned to Spain under the 1763 Treaty of Paris' in February 1763, and handed to O'Reilly in April 1763), so the year only is recorded. The kingdom-of-great-britain dossier (eu-11) should carry the mirror occupation.
10 October 1868: the Ten Years' War begins. 'On 10 October 1868, sugar mill owner Carlos Manuel de Céspedes and his followers proclaimed independence.'

region.text: Camagüey and Ciego de Ávila: 'on 4 November 1868, Camagüey rose up in arms during the Las Clavellinas Uprising'

ledger.note: 4 November 1868: Camagüey rises. 'on 4 November 1868, Camagüey rose up in arms during the Las Clavellinas Uprising'. The page says the province rose; it does not say the rebels held it, so the contest is the researcher's reading; republic-of-cuba-in-arms-ten-years-war carries it as a gain at the same date.

region.text: Las Villas: 'in early February 1869, Las Villas followed'

ledger.note: February 1869: Las Villas rises. 'in early February 1869, Las Villas followed'; the page adds 'The uprising was not supported in the westernmost provinces of Pinar del Río, Havana and Matanzas', which is why the contest stops east of Matanzas.
10 February 1878: the Pact of Zanjón ends the Ten Years' War. 'it was signed on 10 February 1878, by a negotiating committee'; the Little War followed in 1879-80.
10 February 1878: the Pact of Zanjón ends the war in Camagüey and Ciego de Ávila too. 'it was signed on 10 February 1878, by a negotiating committee'.
10 February 1878: the Pact of Zanjón ends the war in Las Villas too. 'it was signed on 10 February 1878, by a negotiating committee'.

region.text: Oriente and Camagüey, the east held by the insurgents of the Cuban War of Independence

ledger.note: 1895: the Cuban War of Independence begins. The page lists the 'Cuban War of Independence' (1895-1898) with the 1895 start; the day (24 February 1895) is in the cuban-nationalists dossier, not on this page.

1897: the autonomy charter 'technically' ends the Captaincy General. The page: the 1897 Constitución Autonómica was 'technically bringing the Captaincy General to an end'; the Spanish administration continued until 1898.

region.text: Santiago de Cuba, 'capturing Santiago de Cuba on July 17'; the same page says Cuba was 'occupied since July 17, 1898' under US military government, which the united-states-of-america dossier draws as the whole island

ledger.note: 17 July 1898: the United States takes Santiago de Cuba. 'capturing Santiago de Cuba on July 17'; the page dates the first American landings to 10 June (Guantánamo Bay) and 22-24 June (Daiquirí and Siboney, east of Santiago), and says Cuba was 'occupied since July 17, 1898' under US military government. The drawn land is the province of Santiago de Cuba, where the city lies, because the page names no other place; the united-states-of-america dossier (am-07) draws the whole island with counterpart spanish-empire. Confidence 2: the date is the page's, the extent is the researcher's reading.
10 December 1898: the Treaty of Paris ends Spanish rule. Infobox 'Treaty of Paris: December 10 1898'.

region.text: Santiago de Cuba, the land taken on 17 July 1898, ending as Spanish Cuba ends

ledger.note: 10 December 1898: the occupation of Spanish Cuba ends with the Treaty of Paris (infobox 'Treaty of Paris: December 10 1898'); the land passes to the Military Government of Cuba at the loss below.

region.text: the island of Cuba, whose sovereignty Spain gives up without ceding it

ledger.note: 10 December 1898: Spain gives up Cuba to nobody. Treaty of Paris page: 'Spain relinquished all claims of sovereignty over and title to Cuba.'; 'Upon Spain's departure, Cuba was to be occupied by the United States'; signed 10 December 1898, in force 11 April 1899. Infobox 'Treaty of Paris: December 10 1898' and successor '1898: Military Government of Cuba'; the page says 'the United States took control of the island'. fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): the counterpart was united-states-of-america, which drew Cuba as US-owned land from December 1898, with the Republic of Cuba (born 1902) 'occupying' it by the reversed-roles rule when united-states-of-america/ledger/83 opened the occupation; sovereignty was relinquished, not ceded, so the cells go to nobody and ledger/83 (occupation of land of the future Republic of Cuba, counterpart republic-of-cuba) puts them under US occupation until independence. The US occupation of Santiago since July is the occupation pair above. The Spanish-American War page says the treaty 'relinquishes sovereignty over Cuba' without ceding it.
December 1898: the Captaincy General of Cuba ends in the Military Government of Cuba.

wars.name: Ten Years' War
wars.outcome: Spanish victory by the Pact of Zanjón on 10 February 1878; infobox end 28 May 1878.
wars.note: The republic-of-cuba-in-arms-ten-years-war dossier carries the rebel side; the zones here are the same lands (repair 2026-10-19). The western provinces of Pinar del Río, Havana and Matanzas did not rise.

wars.name: Little War
wars.outcome: The page lists the Little War (1879-80) among the conflicts; it gives no result and no territory.
wars.note: Listed only; no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Cuban War of Independence

zones.text: the east held by the insurgents

wars.outcome: The war ends with the Treaty of Paris of 10 December 1898; the 1897 autonomy charter 'technically' ended the Captaincy General.
wars.note: The cuban-nationalists dossier (am-08-h) carries the rebel side.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the frontier; the pages describe no land frontier.

sources.title: Captaincy General of Cuba
sources.note: Created 1607, capital Havana, 1764 restructuring with Florida and Louisiana, Little War 1879-80, 1895 war, 1897 autonomy charter, Treaty of Paris 10 December 1898, successor Military Government of Cuba. Reopened 2026-10-19: British capture of Havana (1762) and one-year occupation of the west, return in the Treaty of Paris (1763).

sources.title: Ten Years' War
sources.note: 10 October 1868 and 10 February 1878; Camagüey rose on 4 November 1868; Las Villas in early February 1869; the west did not rise.

sources.title: Republic of Cuba in Arms
sources.note: Opened for the rebel side; no event of this dossier rests on it.

sources.title: Spanish–American War
sources.note: Santiago de Cuba captured 17 July 1898; Cuba 'occupied since July 17, 1898' under US military government; landings 10 June and 22-24 June; Protocol of Peace 12 August; Treaty of Paris 10 December 1898; the page does not give the 1 January 1899 transfer.

sources.title: Siege of Havana
sources.note: Siege from 6 June, honours of war 13 August, British entry 14 August 1762; Havana returned in February 1763 (Treaty of Paris) or handed over in April 1763 (the page gives both); names no other town held by the British. Cited in the notes of ledger events, not as an event source.

sources.title: Treaty of Paris (1898)
sources.note: 'Spain relinquished all claims of sovereignty over and title to Cuba'; 'Upon Spain's departure, Cuba was to be occupied by the United States'; signed 10 December 1898, in force 11 April 1899.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for colonial Cuba (presumably inside the Spanish Empire and Kingdom of Spain rows, whose dossiers are written by am-06 and eu-12; not checked shape by shape). This is the colony alone, type colony, family iberia; the 1607 start rests on the infobox and a one-line statement in the body, and the pages give no limits in 1607 and no event between 1607 and 1762 except the 1764 restructuring (Florida and Louisiana added; no end dates on the page, so no vassal events are written, to avoid an unpaired start).
Repair 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): (1) added the British capture of Havana and occupation of the west, 1762-1763 (occupation_start 1762-08, occupation_end 1763, counterpart kingdom-of-great-britain, confidence 2; the Captaincy page gives the year and 'the western part of the island', the Siege of Havana page gives 13-14 August 1762 and two conflicting return dates, so the end has no month; the extent Havana, Artemisa and Mayabeque is a reading). The kingdom-of-great-britain dossier (eu-11) needs the mirror events. (2) The Ten Years' War contest now covers Oriente (1868-10), Camagüey and Ciego de Ávila (1868-11) and Las Villas (1869-02) to 1878-02, as the rebel dossier gains and contests them. (3) Added the US occupation of Santiago de Cuba from 1898-07 (counterpart united-states-of-america) with its end at the Treaty of Paris; the December 1898 event stays a loss to the US because the page names the Military Government of Cuba as successor; the united-states-of-america dossier records the same month as an occupation, not a gain, and draws the July occupation as the whole island, so the two differ in extent and in type: a point for the reviewer of am-07 and am-06, not changed here.
Still open: the 1897 autonomy is dated by year only (the page gives no month); the 1 January 1899 transfer and the Military Government of Cuba (1898-1902) are not written: a gap-filler could add 'Military Government of Cuba' (1898-1902). The Teller Amendment is not on the pages opened.
